A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA versus full fine-tuning study. All 21 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoBERTa fine-tuning, spectral analyses, continual-learning experiments and pre-training pseudo-loss measurements, including appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original empirical analyses, including singular-vector interventions, learning-rate sweeps, a five-seed experiment and comparisons with LoRA variants.

M1.justification: The LoRA training formulation and intruder detector remain, but v2 adds a central post-fine-tuning procedure that rescales the highest-ranked intruder dimension in each weight matrix. This extends the work from detecting structural differences to modifying models to reduce forgetting (Section 5, Appendix G).

E1.justification: v2 retains the six classification tasks and Alpaca, MetaMath and Magicoder coverage. It adds analysis of continued-pretraining checkpoints using StarCoder and OpenWebMath, and behavioral evaluations using HumanEval, GSM8K, HellaSwag and ARC-Challenge, substantially expanding the evaluated data and scenarios (Figure 6; Appendices B and K).

E2.justification: v2 actually evaluates AdaLoRA, LoRA+, PiSSA and VeRA against vanilla LoRA and full fine-tuning (Figure 23, Appendix O); v1 largely discusses variants without these comparisons. The new scaling experiments also evaluate neighboring pre-trained singular vectors as controls.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled learning-rate sweeps, singular-value scaling sweeps with neighboring-vector controls, and LLaMA behavioral evaluation protocols. Its stated RoBERTa rank sweep and accuracy tables omit r=768, although that rank remains in appendix analyses. The existing alpha settings and continual-learning task order are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds interventions testing whether intruders cause forgetting, learning-rate and correlation analyses, seed robustness, variant comparisons, and spectral tracking of intruder accumulation during continual learning. These substantially extend the evidence beyond v1's observational analyses. Alpha, dataset-size, effective-rank and B-only investigations already existed in v1.

E5.justification: v2 introduces a dedicated five-seed RoBERTa/MNLI experiment and Spearman correlations with p-values for forgetting and task accuracy in both model families (Section 4, Appendices F and N). v1 lacks these statistical checks. This does not establish repeated runs for all retained result tables.

E6.justification: Table 2's accuracies are replaced: full fine-tuning on MNLI changes from 0.8617 to 0.8745. Main forgetting and continual-learning results also change, while r=768 accuracy rows disappear. New intervention results include QQP r=8 at lambda=0.7 showing approximately unchanged accuracy and 33.2% less induced forgetting (Table 3). These are revised or newly reported results, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 newly formalizes the spectral intervention as W = W0 + ΔW + (lambda − 1)u_iσ_iv_i^T and specifies its removal, identity and amplification cases. The original intruder definition, high-dimensional cosine argument and gradient derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds greater forgetting in some LoRA settings and the preference for higher-rank, rank-stabilized models. v2 foregrounds less forgetting even at comparable task accuracy, with hyperparameter exceptions, and makes causal localization of forgetting and mitigation through intruder scaling central contributions. These substantially revise the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 explains continual-learning degradation through accumulating intruders and recommends selecting equally accurate models with fewer intruders and retaining separate adapters. It adds a learning-rate tradeoff between convergence and forgetting, and explains why removing the top intruder does not restore the pre-trained model (Appendices A and G).

D1.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation-harness names, A100 hardware specifications and training/evaluation timings. Appendix K expands checkpoint documentation and replaces the Magicoder-named identifiers in v1's MetaMath rows with MetaMath identifiers. However, v2 omits v1's explicit bias/LayerNorm-training statement, leaving that implementation detail less clear.

R1.justification: v1 positions its forgetting observations partly against Biderman et al., discussing differences in task fit. v2 explicitly positions itself as extending their finding to comparable task accuracy. It also expands positioning around LoRA variants and adapter management, adding discussion of LoRA+, MiLoRA, ReFT and S-LoRA.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, behavioral narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The former main-text explanation of intruder origins moves to Appendix A, while a new causal-intervention section takes its place. Numerous appendix sections are reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively restructures displays: forgetting bar charts become line plots, continual-learning results are combined with spectral maps, effective-rank figures are consolidated, and the detector becomes a numbered algorithm. New intervention tables and correlation, seed and variant figures add substantial visual content.

improvement.justification: Controlled intruder-scaling experiments with neighboring-vector comparisons address an important weakness in v1's mainly correlational explanation of forgetting (Section 5, Appendix G). Learning-rate, seed and variant analyses further test that explanation, and implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. Some replaced RoBERTa results and retained r=768 appendix analyses remain insufficiently reconciled, but these reporting gaps do not outweigh the substantial gain in direct mechanistic evidence.
